payload.title: Closed-Loop Multiplicity Calibration for Additive Count Mass
plain_method_steps: Read only physically separated, feature-only supplied pose tracks and retain the supplied identity slots solely for routing.

Construct deterministic synthetic motion atoms from short pose segments followed by a smooth return path; repeat each atom one to four times under disclosed crop, masking, and monotone-resampling transforms.

Train a compact temporal filter to emit nonnegative interval count mass, using the known synthetic multiplicity for absolute calibration and cut-additivity and transformed-view consistency as auxiliary constraints.
At inference, sum interval mass once per supplied identity; expose transformation disagreement as a failure score rather than selecting a period.
payload.core_hypothesis: Known multiplicity of synthetic closed pose loops can calibrate an additive event-mass measure that transfers to real repetitions without learner access to real per-person count, density, period, or boundary labels.
payload.cheap_kill_gate: Using only checksum-frozen feature-only train/validation tracks, freeze a held-out synthetic-loop pack before fitting. Kill if multiplicity MAE over one-to-four repeats exceeds 0.15 cycles, median random-cut additivity error exceeds 5%, or time-shuffled non-loop controls receive more than 0.25 median count mass. Evaluator labels remain unopened.
payload.expected_contribution: A bounded study of selector-free absolute count calibration through synthetic loop multiplicity and measure additivity on supplied pose tracks; synthetic correspondence supervision and external pose/tracker supervision would be disclosed.
payload.risk: Synthetic return paths may be too unlike semantic repetitions, and the learner may recognize construction seams instead of transferable motion closure.
closest_prior_boundary: RepNet already uses synthetic repetitions; synthetic repetition construction is not a contribution by itself.
PAMS already covers self-supervised skeleton periodic learning and localized tempo perturbations; the boundary is additive count-mass calibration without a pseudo-period selector.
MultiCounter+ already establishes robust identity-indexed MRAC and external detection/tracking machinery.
DeepPhase already occupies unsupervised motion phase, while TWCRAC occupies local cycle-consistency territory; neither phase learning nor local consistency is claimed.

payload.title: Band-Marginalized Limb-Phase Synchronization
plain_method_steps: Transform root-centered joint velocities with a fixed complex wavelet bank spanning the admissible temporal scales, retaining every band rather than selecting a period.
Create a confidence-weighted graph whose nodes are limb-band analytic phases and whose edges encode stable phase offsets, including allowed anti-phase relations.
Solve an SO(2) synchronization problem per window, then marginalize angular current across bands according to graph residuals instead of choosing one spectral peak.
Integrate the reliable consensus current per supplied identity and emit an abstention flag when graph connectivity, circular concentration, or cross-band agreement is inadequate.
payload.core_hypothesis: Repetitive motion produces mutually consistent phase currents across several limbs even when any single limb or frequency band locks to a half or double harmonic; marginal synchronization can therefore count more reliably than a hard period selector.
payload.cheap_kill_gate: On a newly specified, immutable pose-only diagnostic pack derived from frozen train/validation feature distributions, test chirps, pauses, anti-phase limbs, half/double harmonics, missing joints, and nonperiodic distractors. Kill if median winding error exceeds 10%, harmonic locking exceeds 5%, or the failure flag detects fewer than 80% of ambiguous cases at 10% false alarms. This pack must not modify or reinterpret the killed WARP-PHASE fixtures.
payload.expected_contribution: A selector-free multichannel signal-fusion hypothesis for supplied-track repetition counting, with an explicit reliability output based on circular synchronization residuals.
payload.risk: Limb phases can be weak, intermittent, or genuinely multi-rate, causing cancellation or confident synchronization to a nonsemantic motion component.
closest_prior_boundary: DeepPhase already learns local multichannel motion phase; the possible distinction is fixed-band cross-limb synchronization and reliability, not unsupervised phase itself.
PAMS already uses period-adaptive multiscale consistency and inference consensus; marginal graph synchronization must be compared directly and not described as the first multiscale pose method.
TWCRAC already covers local cycle consistency and nonstationary motion; no local-window or dynamic-tempo novelty claim is permitted.
MultiCounter+ already covers identity-indexed variable-period MRAC; supplied tracking remains external supervision.

payload.title: Conditioned Hankel Pole-Path Posterior
plain_method_steps: Form confidence-masked multichannel block-Hankel matrices from each supplied identity's normalized pose velocities.
Use total-least-squares matrix pencils to estimate damped complex poles and attach rank-gap, residual, and condition-number diagnostics to every pole.
Link compatible poles across overlapping windows with a bounded dynamic program and represent fundamentals and integer-related harmonics as a posterior family rather than a single selected period.
Integrate posterior expected angular frequency to obtain a continuous count and widen or abstain when the subspace is ill-conditioned or competing paths remain unresolved.
payload.core_hypothesis: A low-rank pole model can track nonstationary repetition rates while exposing mathematical non-identifiability, allowing harmonic ambiguity to become reported uncertainty instead of a brittle hard decision.
payload.cheap_kill_gate: Run a CPU-only frozen diagnostic suite containing pose-shaped damped oscillations, smooth and abrupt chirps, harmonic mixtures, missing samples, and matched aperiodic motion. Kill if well-conditioned cases exceed 10% integrated-count error, fewer than 85% of deliberately ill-conditioned cases are flagged, or perturbing valid pose coordinates within the frozen noise envelope changes count by more than 10%.
payload.expected_contribution: A failure-aware subspace signal-processing baseline for per-identity supplied-track counting, emphasizing pole-path uncertainty rather than learned period supervision.
payload.risk: Human motion may violate the short-window low-rank oscillator model, and matrix-pencil estimates can be unstable under severe missingness or closely spaced modes.
closest_prior_boundary: Runia et al. and RepNet already establish nonstationary spectral or time-varying-period estimation; spectral estimation itself is not claimed.
PAMS already covers multiscale pose periodic learning, and DeepPhase already covers local motion-phase manifolds.
TWCRAC's local nonstationary formulation remains an unresolved boundary, so the claim must stay at conditioned pole tracking and abstention.
MultiCounter+ supplies the MRAC task boundary; this candidate neither detects nor tracks people.

payload.title: Leave-One-Person-Out Common-Mode Cancellation
plain_method_steps: Align all supplied person tracks on their frozen source-frame clock and compute confidence-masked root-centered pose velocities.
For each target identity, estimate a robust low-rank common-motion subspace from the other identities only, with explicit guards for one-person scenes and insufficient overlap.
Subtract only the component that is coherent across multiple people and joint groups, then pass the residual and untouched target signal through the same frozen label-restricted counter.
Report nuisance attenuation, target-signal preservation, and changes in untouched identities; never feed person identifiers or evaluator labels to the model.
payload.core_hypothesis: Camera motion and scene-wide nuisance often occupy a cross-person common subspace, while true repetition evidence remains identity-specific; leave-one-person-out cancellation can improve counting without erasing the target's motion.
payload.cheap_kill_gate: On frozen feature-only train/validation tracks, inject checksum-frozen shared translation, scale, and low-frequency camera trajectories plus independent person-specific oscillations. Kill if common nuisance is attenuated by less than 15 dB, target oscillatory energy preservation falls below 90%, or changing one person's trajectory alters another person's residual by more than 1%.
payload.expected_contribution: A multi-person signal-separation study linking robust common-mode rejection to supplied-track repetition counting and cross-person interference diagnostics.
payload.risk: People may intentionally move synchronously, so genuine action energy can enter the common subspace; many videos may also contain too few overlapping identities for stable decomposition.
closest_prior_boundary: MultiCounter+ already uses spatial-temporal consistency and identity-indexed MRAC; cross-person common-mode cancellation must not be framed as identity-consistency novelty.
PAMS supplies a strong pose-periodic downstream baseline; any benefit must be isolated to the nuisance-removal front end.
DeepPhase is not displaced because this candidate does not claim a new phase representation.
TWCRAC's local periodic statistics are separate; no dynamic-threshold or local-cycle claim is made.

payload.title: Fragment-Boundary Transport for Count-Mass Conservation
plain_method_steps: Freeze a label-restricted supplied-track base response model and treat its architecture and periodic representation as non-contributions.
Create deterministic feature-only cuts, gaps, and re-entry patterns from each complete training track while preserving the supplied identity routing key.

Learn a small boundary transport operator from endpoint pose and velocity states so that intact response mass equals fragment mass plus an explicit boundary correction; use wrong-identity endpoint pairings as negatives.
At inference, compose fragment masses only when the transport residual is small and otherwise emit an abstention or interval rather than silently joining them.
payload.core_hypothesis: Most fragmentation error is localized at missing boundaries and can be represented as a transport correction between endpoint motion states, enabling count-mass conservation without real count or period labels.
payload.cheap_kill_gate: Using frozen feature-only train/validation tracks and predeclared cut patterns, kill if unseen-cut reconstruction error exceeds 5% of intact response mass, wrong-identity pairings receive more than 10% of correct boundary weight, the endpoint code collapses below a frozen effective-rank floor, or one-person cuts alter byte-identical untouched-person outputs.
payload.expected_contribution: A failure-aware, supplied-track fragmentation mechanism and conservation diagnostic; the base counter, supplied identities, and external tracking supervision remain explicitly attributed.
payload.risk: A self-consistency objective can preserve a biased base counter, while long gaps or large tempo changes may make boundary correction fundamentally unidentifiable.
closest_prior_boundary: MultiCounter+ already addresses tracking and temporal consistency; this candidate is not a tracking or re-identification contribution.
PAMS and DeepPhase may instantiate the frozen base response, but their periodic representations are not claimed.
TWCRAC already covers time-window-cycle consistency, so the residual claim is boundary transport under synthetic fragmentation rather than window consistency.
Any later predicted-track study would require separate tracking metrics; this bounded candidate remains supplied-track only.

payload.title: Persistent-Cohomology Crossing Ensemble
plain_method_steps: Build delay embeddings of confidence-masked pose velocities separately for each supplied identity and several fixed joint subsets.
Compute persistent one-dimensional cohomology and derive circular coordinates only for loops whose persistence and neighborhood support pass frozen numerical checks.
Count signed crossings through an ensemble of data-derived Poincare sections, then aggregate section counts with a median and expose section disagreement as uncertainty.
Use no learned period, count, density, or cycle-boundary label; tracks without a persistent loop receive an abstention rather than a forced count.
payload.core_hypothesis: A genuine repetitive action traces a stable loop in delay-embedded pose space, so topological winding and section-crossing agreement can count repetitions without selecting a temporal period and can fail visibly on non-loop motion.
payload.cheap_kill_gate: On deterministic synthetic loops embedded in frozen train/validation pose noise and on pose-only time-warp, reversal, crop, and shuffled-time controls, kill if median crossing error exceeds 0.25 cycles, monotone resampling changes winding by more than 2%, shuffled-time false loops exceed 5%, or fewer than 80% of deliberately non-loop tracks abstain.
payload.expected_contribution: A selector-free topological counting hypothesis with an explicit identifiability certificate for supplied pose tracks.
payload.risk: Real actions can form open, self-intersecting, drifting, or multi-loop trajectories; persistent topology may also be computationally heavy and sensitive to embedding choices.
closest_prior_boundary: DeepPhase already occupies unsupervised local motion-phase manifolds; the narrow distinction is persistent-loop crossing with an abstention certificate, not phase discovery.
PAMS already covers self-supervised skeleton periodic representation and tempo robustness; identical supplied-track comparisons are required.
TWCRAC already covers local cycles and nonstationarity; no first-cycle or local-window claim is permitted.
MultiCounter+ establishes per-person MRAC, while the supplied pose/tracker pipeline remains external supervision.

payload.title: Set-Valued Counting Under Pose Missingness
plain_method_steps: Estimate train-only kinematic uncertainty sets from feature-side bone-length and velocity statistics, without opening evaluator labels.
Propagate observed joints and missing-coordinate intervals through a fixed multiband analytic-response bank to obtain lower and upper interval response mass.

Aggregate interval mass once per supplied identity, preserving inclusion under nested missingness masks and returning a count interval plus a point estimate only when the interval is sufficiently narrow.
Keep externally supervised pose and tracking explicit, and evaluate missingness severity and interval width separately from count accuracy.
payload.core_hypothesis: For incomplete pose, a defensible interval of repetition counts is more scientifically reliable than imputation followed by an overconfident point count, and useful bounds can be obtained from kinematic uncertainty without per-person labels.
payload.cheap_kill_gate: Apply nested deterministic masks to frozen feature-only train/validation tracks. Kill if interval nesting is violated in any audited case, the unmasked estimate is contained in fewer than 95% of masked intervals, median width exceeds 1.5 cycles at 30% missing joints, or width fails to increase monotonically with missingness. No evaluator label is needed for this gate.
payload.expected_contribution: A failure-aware partial-identification protocol and signal-processing construction for supplied-track repetition counting under pose dropout, with final validation labels used only after predictions and intervals are frozen.
payload.risk: Valid uncertainty sets may be too wide for practical counting, while empirically tight sets may not cover unobserved motion and could give misleading guarantees.
closest_prior_boundary: SSTRAC and related work already study skeleton repair and occlusion robustness; this candidate claims neither repair nor missing-pose novelty, only set-valued count propagation.
MultiCounter+ already addresses robust MRAC and identity consistency.
PAMS supplies the pose-periodic comparison boundary, and DeepPhase supplies the unsupervised phase boundary.
TWCRAC already covers local nonstationary statistics; dynamic thresholds and local windows are not contributions here.

payload.title: Masked Multi-Horizon Pose-Delta Prediction
plain_method_steps: Normalize each supplied person track into hip-centered, scale-normalized pose coordinates while retaining fixed visibility masks and sampled-frame timing only.
Mask contiguous joint-time blocks and encode the remaining pose sequence with a track-local temporal encoder.
Predict signed pose deltas at several fixed past and future horizons, using confidence-weighted reconstruction without count, period, density, or boundary targets.
Freeze the encoder and expose the same representation to a fixed-capacity downstream RAC readout for every comparator.
Run preregistered objective, shortcut, collapse, and cross-identity isolation checks before any efficacy experiment.
payload.core_hypothesis: Multi-horizon signed motion prediction can make repetition-relevant dynamics linearly accessible without committing to a hard period selector or supplying learner-side count/period labels.
payload.cheap_kill_gate: On checksum-frozen, source-disjoint, feature/label-isolated train/val splits, stop if masked-delta error does not beat constant-pose, linear-interpolation, and constant-velocity baselines; if clock-only, mask-pattern, or temporal-shuffle probes retain more than 20% of the full objective gain; if embedding effective rank falls below the preregistered floor; or if perturbing one non-target identity changes an untouched target embedding beyond the fixed numerical tolerance.
payload.expected_contribution: A bounded label-free pose representation objective that tests whether multi-scale signed dynamics, rather than explicit period selection, are sufficient for supplied-track multi-person RAC.
payload.risk: The objective may reward generic smooth-motion forecasting, and fixed horizons may miss very long or strongly nonstationary repetitions.
closest_prior_boundary: MultiCounter+ already owns supplied-track multi-person RAC, per-person outputs, temporal consistency, and long/short-period awareness; the proposed novelty is only the label-free representation objective.
PAMS already owns self-supervised skeleton periodic learning and period-adaptive multi-scale consistency; this candidate uses fixed prediction horizons and no inference-time period consensus.
DeepPhase already owns unsupervised local phase manifolds and reconstruction; this candidate predicts signed kinematic deltas without an explicit phase manifold.
Motion Feature Learning/TSSM already uses temporal self-similarity reconstruction; no TSSM reconstruction or similarity matrix is claimed here.
RepNet already uses synthetic resampling, TSSM, and per-frame period/periodicity prediction; none of those targets are used.

TWCRAC already covers pose, local windows, temporal cycle consistency, and nonstationary motion; this candidate is limited to masked multi-horizon delta prediction and requires a mechanism-matched comparison.

payload.title: Cross-View Kinematic Residual Denoising
plain_method_steps: Derive two deterministic views of each supplied track: normalized joint coordinates and a kinematic view of bones, angles, velocities, and accelerations.
Corrupt complementary joint-time regions independently in the two views without changing sampled-frame timing.
Use one shared track-local encoder to reconstruct only cross-view kinematic residuals that are unavailable from the same corrupted view.
Exclude count, period, density, boundary, person-count, and cross-track targets from learner inputs and losses.
Freeze the representation and run the full preregistered kill suite before downstream RAC evaluation.
payload.core_hypothesis: Cross-view residual denoising can emphasize articulated cyclic dynamics while making direct coordinate copying and visibility-pattern shortcuts measurably unhelpful.
payload.cheap_kill_gate: On checksum-frozen, source-disjoint, feature/label-isolated train/val splits, stop if cross-view residual error does not beat direct masked-coordinate, static-pose, and per-joint interpolation baselines; if static-shape, visibility-mask, or clock-only probes recover more than 20% of the full gain; if variance/effective-rank collapse crosses the preregistered bound; or if corrupting another identity changes the byte-identical target representation beyond tolerance.
payload.expected_contribution: A representation-level test of whether complementary skeletal parameterizations provide repetition-sensitive supervision without period labels or a self-similarity selector.
payload.risk: Coordinate and kinematic views are algebraically coupled, so the task may remain too easy unless corruption removes direct reconstruction paths.
closest_prior_boundary: MultiCounter+ owns the multi-person supplied-track task setting; this candidate changes only track-local pretraining.
PAMS owns self-supervised skeleton periodic learning and period-adaptive consistency; this objective is cross-view residual denoising with no period estimate.
DeepPhase owns unsupervised phase-oriented reconstruction; no phase variable or local phase manifold is imposed.
Motion Feature Learning/TSSM owns motion-feature and temporal-similarity reconstruction territory; the candidate reconstructs kinematic residuals rather than a TSSM.
RepNet owns TSSM and period/periodicity prediction with synthetic resampling; those mechanisms are excluded.
TWCRAC overlaps on pose and local temporal modeling; novelty remains bounded to complementary-view corruption and residual prediction.

payload.title: Track-Exclusive Overlap Bootstrap Consistency
plain_method_steps: Sample two overlapping temporal crops from the same supplied identity track using only source indices and fixed augmentations.
Encode one crop with a student and the other with an exponential-moving-average teacher, aligning only their shared physical frames.
Predict teacher embeddings for the overlap while giving the two branches different boundary context and pose masking.
Keep queues, normalization statistics, and teacher updates private to the track during each training item so no co-actor metadata enters the objective.
Freeze the encoder and audit objective gain, shortcut predictability, collapse, and identity isolation on the frozen split manifest.
payload.core_hypothesis: Agreement on shared motion under differing temporal context can learn stable repetition-relevant state without identifying a discrete cycle or exposing period/count labels.
payload.cheap_kill_gate: On checksum-frozen, source-disjoint, feature/label-isolated train/val splits, stop if overlap prediction does not beat identity-copy, recency, and untrained-teacher baselines; if crop offset, absolute clock, track length, or padding probes explain more than 20% of the gain; if teacher/student variance or effective rank violates the frozen collapse bounds; or if swapping every non-target track changes the untouched target embedding beyond tolerance.
payload.expected_contribution: A track-exclusive self-distillation objective for temporal state stability whose usefulness can be falsified before any full RAC training.
payload.risk: Bootstrap consistency can converge to low-information features, and overlap alignment may favor pose identity over motion structure.
closest_prior_boundary: MultiCounter+ already uses per-person tracks and temporal consistency; the candidate claims only a particular label-free overlap-bootstrap representation objective.
PAMS owns self-supervised periodic skeleton consistency and inference consensus; no period-adaptive scale or consensus is used.
DeepPhase owns local phase-manifold learning; overlap agreement does not define phase coordinates.
Motion Feature Learning/TSSM owns temporal self-similarity reconstruction; this candidate aligns embeddings only on identical physical frames.
RepNet owns TSSM, resampling, and explicit periodicity/period outputs; all are absent.
TWCRAC owns intra-video temporal cycle consistency and local windows; the distinction is exact-frame overlap bootstrap consistency, which needs mechanism-matched adjudication.

payload.title: Motion-Arrow Factorized Representation
plain_method_steps: Create forward and time-reversed versions of each normalized supplied track with identical visibility and timing metadata.
Encode each sequence into a reversal-invariant motion-content subspace and a signed motion-arrow subspace.
Train content agreement across reversal while predicting local velocity direction only from the arrow subspace.
Penalize cross-covariance between the two subspaces and never infer a period, cycle boundary, count, or density target.
Freeze both subspaces and apply reversal, clock, collapse, and per-identity intervention checks before downstream use.
payload.core_hypothesis: Separating what motion recurs from which temporal direction it follows can yield a more useful RAC representation than a brittle hard period decision.
payload.cheap_kill_gate: On checksum-frozen, source-disjoint, feature/label-isolated train/val splits, stop if content agreement and arrow prediction do not beat pooled-pose and local-velocity baselines; if absolute clock, padding edge, or reversal-token probes recover more than 20% of the gain; if either subspace collapses or the two fail the preregistered independence bound; or if reversing one person changes any byte-identical non-target person's representation beyond tolerance.
payload.expected_contribution: A bounded factorization objective that explicitly tests direction/content disentanglement for pose repetition without period supervision.
payload.risk: Time reversal may create physically implausible sequences, and subspace separation may not correspond to repetition structure.
closest_prior_boundary: MultiCounter+ defines the multi-person RAC setting and identity-specific outputs; this proposal remains a per-track representation intervention.
PAMS already uses tempo perturbation and multi-scale consistency; reversal factorization is not presented as period adaptation.
DeepPhase owns unsupervised phase manifolds; the proposed two-subspace representation has no circular phase constraint.
Motion Feature Learning/TSSM owns temporal motion-feature reconstruction; the objective instead factorizes reversal behavior.
RepNet owns synthetic temporal resampling and explicit period/periodicity prediction; reversal is the only temporal intervention here and supplies no period label.
TWCRAC covers nonstationary pose cycles and temporal consistency; the narrowly claimed boundary is direction/content factorization.

payload.title: Predictive-Surprise Repetition Representation
plain_method_steps: Encode each supplied identity track causally from normalized pose, visibility, and sampled-frame gaps only.
Predict a distribution over the next signed pose delta and retain calibrated negative log likelihood as a local surprise channel.
Aggregate latent state and surprise over fixed short windows without peaks, autocorrelation, FFT, or period selection.
Train only the next-delta likelihood and calibration objectives, with no count, period, density, or boundary annotations.
Freeze the representation and test whether any gain survives nonperiodic controls and all isolation checks.
payload.core_hypothesis: Repeated motion may be represented through recurring patterns of predictability and surprise even when no explicit cycle length is selected.
payload.cheap_kill_gate: On checksum-frozen, source-disjoint, feature/label-isolated train/val splits, stop if held-out next-delta likelihood and calibration do not beat last-pose, constant-velocity, and unconditional-motion baselines; if monotonic-motion, shuffled-window, clock-only, or confidence-only controls retain more than 20% of the representation gain; if latent or surprise channels collapse; or if changing a non-target identity alters the untouched target output beyond tolerance.
payload.expected_contribution: A label-free probabilistic motion representation that replaces hard recurrence selection with calibrated local predictive structure.
payload.risk: Surprise may primarily encode occlusion, abrupt camera effects, or tracking noise rather than repetition.
closest_prior_boundary: MultiCounter+ owns supplied-track per-person RAC and temporal modeling; only the predictive-surprise pretext is proposed.
PAMS owns periodic self-supervision and internal tempo perturbation; this candidate uses causal likelihood without tempo-derived consistency.
DeepPhase owns reconstruction-based local phase structure; predictive uncertainty is not claimed as phase estimation.
Motion Feature Learning/TSSM owns motion-feature and similarity reconstruction; no temporal similarity matrix is formed.
RepNet owns per-frame period and periodicity prediction; the surprise channel is not trained against either label.
TWCRAC covers local temporal statistics and dynamic behavior; surprise must be compared directly and claimed only as a representation objective.

payload.title: Identity-Private Soft Loop-Closure Memory
plain_method_steps: Maintain a separate bounded memory bank for each supplied identity track, containing only that track's normalized pose embeddings and source indices.
For each current frame, compute a dense soft distribution over eligible earlier states after a fixed exclusion radius.
Reconstruct the current kinematic residual from the soft memory mixture while regularizing occupancy entropy and memory utilization.
Never take an argmax, locate a peak, estimate a period, harmonic-correct a candidate, or share memory across identities.
Freeze the encoder and memory rule, then audit reconstruction, shortcuts, collapse, and byte-level identity isolation.
payload.core_hypothesis: A differentiable distribution over earlier matching states can encode recurrence evidence without reproducing the terminally failed hard selector.
payload.cheap_kill_gate: On checksum-frozen, source-disjoint, feature/label-isolated train/val splits, stop if residual reconstruction does not beat fixed-recency, uniform-memory, and kernel-smoothing baselines; if absolute clock, memory age, track length, or confidence probes explain more than 20% of the gain; if memory occupancy or embedding effective rank crosses preregistered collapse bounds; or if byte-changing another identity's memory changes the untouched target output at all beyond the fixed numerical tolerance.
payload.expected_contribution: A strictly soft, identity-private recurrence representation with explicit evidence that it is neither a hidden hard period selector nor a shared-state shortcut.
payload.risk: The memory may collapse to recency or generic pose similarity, and dense matching may be computationally expensive for long tracks.
closest_prior_boundary: MultiCounter+ owns identity-specific multi-person RAC; the proposed distinction is byte-isolated per-track soft recurrence memory.
PAMS owns inference-time configuration consensus and period-adaptive consistency; this memory never emits or selects a period.
DeepPhase owns local phase manifolds and reconstruction; soft loop closure is not claimed as phase discovery.
Motion Feature Learning/TSSM owns temporal self-similarity reconstruction; pairwise similarity is an operator here, not a standalone novelty claim.
RepNet owns TSSM and explicit periodicity estimation; no TSSM head, resampling supervision, or hard periodic output is used.
TWCRAC owns time-window cycles and temporal cycle consistency; the candidate boundary is identity-private dense soft memory with no cycle decision.

payload.title: Cross-Person Nuisance-Rejected Track Encoding
plain_method_steps: Choose one supplied target identity and keep its pose bytes, visibility, and sampled-frame indices identical across two constructed views.
Independently swap, drop, reorder, or tempo-perturb only the non-target tracks while preserving the target input exactly.
Train the target encoder for counterfactual embedding invariance together with a target-local masked signed-delta objective.
Adversarially suppress recoverability of person count and co-actor summary cues from the target embedding without exposing RAC labels.
Freeze the model and verify target objective utility, nuisance rejection, noncollapse, and strict identity isolation on source-disjoint data.
payload.core_hypothesis: Explicit counterfactual invariance to co-actor changes can prevent multi-person context leakage while preserving target-local dynamics useful for per-person RAC.
payload.cheap_kill_gate: On checksum-frozen, source-disjoint, feature/label-isolated train/val splits, stop if the target-local masked-delta objective does not beat static and constant-velocity baselines; if person-count, co-actor-motion, clock, or augmentation-signature probes exceed preregistered chance-plus-margin bounds; if target embeddings collapse under the invariance loss; or if any permitted non-target intervention changes the byte-identical target representation beyond tolerance.
payload.expected_contribution: A representation-level identity-isolation mechanism and falsifiable audit for supplied-track multi-person RAC, coupled to a label-free target-local motion objective.
payload.risk: Aggressive nuisance rejection may discard genuinely useful interaction context, while imperfect track independence could make the intervention unrealistic.
closest_prior_boundary: MultiCounter+ owns multi-person identity-aware RAC; this candidate focuses narrowly on counterfactual removal of co-actor leakage from each target representation.
PAMS owns self-supervised skeleton periodic learning; the auxiliary target objective is masked delta prediction rather than period-adaptive consistency.
DeepPhase owns unsupervised phase manifolds; no phase topology is imposed.
Motion Feature Learning/TSSM owns motion-feature and similarity reconstruction; neither is the claimed contribution.
RepNet owns resampling, TSSM, and period/periodicity heads; the non-target tempo perturbation is solely a nuisance intervention and never labels the target.
TWCRAC overlaps on pose, local temporal reasoning, and multi-person RAC context; novelty is bounded to counterfactual co-actor invariance plus an explicit isolation gate.

failure_memory_union: The signed WARP-PHASE warp-integral candidate is terminally killed by immutable Gate-2 counts 246/55/144/50/66. None of these candidates changes its thresholds, fixtures, selector, semantics, or status, and none is a fallback continuation of that method.

The killed branch has zero eligible efficacy results and no training or server authorization. Engineering fixtures, CPU smokes, and self-consistency gates must never be reported as count-performance evidence.

Any future learner must consume physically separated feature-only train data; evaluator count, density, period, and boundary fields remain in a separately permissioned vault. Frozen validation labels may be joined only after predictions and decisions are frozen.

External detector, GT-box assistance, pose-estimator, tracker, supplied identity tracks, synthetic correspondence or multiplicity, and any video-level supervision must be disclosed. The precise ceiling is that the counting learner uses no real per-person count or period labels.
Forbidden language remains: every variant of first, annotation-free, end-to-end, constant-time, and SOTA without eligible protocol-matched evidence.

MultiCounter and MultiCounter+ already establish MRAC, per-person outputs, identity consistency, and variable-period multi-person counting. PAMS already establishes self-supervised pose periodic learning, multiscale consistency, inference consensus, and localized tempo perturbations. DeepPhase already establishes unsupervised local motion phase. TWCRAC already occupies local-window cycle consistency, dynamic local statistics, and nonstationary motion, with full-method overlap unresolved.

All cheap gates above are new candidate-specific, checksum-frozen train/validation feature diagnostics. They cannot reuse, replace, repair, or reinterpret the immutable WARP-PHASE Gate-2 population, and passing them would authorize only further review rather than a claim.
WARP-PHASE is terminally killed at immutable Gate2 by exact observed counts agreement=246, half_overall=55, double_overall=144, symmetric_half=50, and symmetric_double=66; the K5 stop is final.
Do not repair, retune, threshold-adjust, harmonic-correct, rerun, or reuse the failed hard selector, and do not replace its frozen stochastic fixture population.
Any future candidate requires a newly preregistered checksum-frozen, source-disjoint, feature/label-physically-separated train/val protocol before training.

The admissible supervision claim is only that the learner receives no per-person count, period, density, or boundary labels; any externally supplied tracks or other supervision must be disclosed exactly.
MultiCounter and MultiCounter+ already define the multi-person RAC setting, per-person identity outputs, temporal consistency, and long/short-period awareness.
PAMS already covers self-supervised skeleton periodic learning, period-adaptive multi-scale consistency, inference configuration consensus, and internal tempo perturbation.

DeepPhase covers unsupervised local phase manifolds and reconstruction; Motion Feature Learning covers temporal motion features/TSSM reconstruction; RepNet covers TSSM, synthetic resampling, and per-frame period/periodicity prediction.

TWCRAC's accessible boundary includes time-window cycles, intra-video temporal cycle consistency, pose, local statistics, dynamic thresholds, and nonstationary motion; full overlap remains unresolved and requires mechanism-matched checking.
TSSM, masking, local windows, private memory, pose normalization, and standard consistency losses are established operators rather than standalone contributions.

This shard makes no ranking, acceptance, or rejection decision; all seven entries are bounded hypotheses whose objective, shortcut, collapse, and identity-isolation gates must be passed on frozen train/val before efficacy claims.
